findings.evidence: Line 39 reads `@[expose] public section`. `mathlib/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Widesubcategory.lean:26` reads `public section`, with no expose, for the parallel construction.
findings.fix: Use plain `public section`, as Mathlib's `Monoidal/Widesubcategory.lean` does. Prove the characterizing lemmas with `(rfl)` so they stay usable downstream. If a specific body really must stay unfoldable, mark only that declaration `@[expose]`. At minimum, `skeletonMulEquiv` must not be exposed.
findings.issue: `@[expose] public section` publishes every body, including the instance bodies and the noncomputable `skeletonMulEquiv`, which is built by `MulEquiv.ofBijective` with a tactic proof. The rfl simp lemmas (`tensorObj_of`, `whiskerLeft_iso`, `associator_hom_iso`, `inclusion_μ`, `core_μ_iso`, `skeletonMulEquiv_toSkeleton`, …) already characterize this structure, so no consumer needs to unfold these bodies.

findings.evidence: The only lemmas about `skeletonMulEquiv` are `skeletonMulEquiv_toSkeleton` and `skeletonMulEquiv_monoidHom_core`. Neither one mentions `.symm`.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] lemma skeletonMulEquiv_symm_toSkeleton (X : C) : skeletonMulEquiv.symm (toSkeleton X) = toSkeleton (⟨X⟩ : Core C)`. It follows from `skeletonMulEquiv_toSkeleton` by `MulEquiv.symm_apply_eq`.
findings.issue: `skeletonMulEquiv` has an evaluation lemma only in the forward direction (`skeletonMulEquiv_toSkeleton`). Nothing evaluates `skeletonMulEquiv.symm` on a class, so a consumer moving from `Skeleton C` to `Skeleton (Core C)` has to unfold `MulEquiv.ofBijective`.

summary: The API surface is mostly complete and correctly simp-annotated, but `@[expose] public section` publishes every body in the file, including the proof-built `skeletonMulEquiv`, and the inverse of `skeletonMulEquiv` has no evaluation lemma.
